Zona Archeologica — Rome, Italy

🟡 Local press research

Average day Higher caution advised night

In detail

The Zona Archeologica covers the Colosseum, Roman Forum and Palatine Hill - Rome's most visited monuments, thronged with tourists by day. Daytime problems are well documented and persistent: pickpocket crews and scam operations targeting tourists around the Fori Imperiali, with regular police arrests through 2026. More seriously, the area became a recurring flashpoint for youth violence at night: on 2 July 2026 a birthday gathering turned into fireworks and firecracker-throwing chaos among crowds, with three arrests; a dedicated "Piano Roma Notte" police operation and a large blitz followed, identifying over 350 people and making 10 arrests around the Colosseum specifically to curb "baby gang" incidents. Given the recurring, officially targeted violence at night, this is one of the more serious after-dark concerns in Municipio I, while daytime risk is largely limited to theft and scams.
